sentence: This project builds virus-like particles that edit and select blood stem cells directly in patients, aiming to make gene therapy more portable.
This project studies how immune cells made from stem cells can transfer a protein called frataxin to brain cells in Friedreich's ataxia.
This project builds ultrasonic devices that eject living cells from a cell layer without damage so they can be tested by single-cell RNA sequencing.
This project studies which molecular domains of a receptor let Drosophila melanogaster sense temperature.
This project studies how aging and host genetics shape the role of the gut microbiome in cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease.
This project uses whole genome sequencing to test for antimicrobial resistance in sick animals.
This project tries to find out how to make and expand a patient's own limbal stem cells to treat blindness from an opaque cornea.
This project builds a simple, low-cost paper-based microfluidic device that detects several high-risk genotypes for cervical cancer screening at the point of care.
This project studies how circular pieces of DNA outside chromosomes form, work and help cancers resist treatment.
This project studies how the immune system can be used to prevent and treat all types of cancer.
This project builds computer methods that describe alternative splicing from sequencing data and work out the effects of genetic variants.
This project studies how mutation and amplification of two common human oncogenes promote lung adenocarcinomas and small cell lung cancers.
This project studies how hexavalent chromium, a metal that causes lung cancer, leads to chromosome instability.
This project identifies groups of neurons in brain reward circuits and studies how they drive or unleash alcohol- and opioid-seeking behaviors.
This project builds a data-driven algorithm to assign causes to hospitalizations and a tool that spots patients with HIV at higher risk of future hospitalization.
This project builds a platform using patient-derived organoids to measure how cancer cells respond to and resist chemotherapy.
This project develops simpler and more reliable ways to analyze data on the microbes in the human body.
This project builds a wearable sensor system that uses machine learning to detect when people use buprenorphine.
This project tries to find out which T-cell subsets, molecular mechanisms and antigens cause heart inflammation after immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
This project studies how RNA recoding changes the function of proteins involved in intracellular transport and DNA replication and repair.
